newsitem.title: ITALY: Daughter of Lancia car founder stabbed to death.
newsitem.headline: Daughter of Lancia car founder stabbed to death.

text.p: The 70-year-old daughter of the founder of the Lancia car company was stabbed to death at her villa in northern Italy on Friday and police said the woman's daughter was suspected of the attack.

Eleonara Maria Lancia, whose father Vincenzo founded the company in 1906, was found dead at the luxury villa, set in secluded hills on the outskirts of Italy's car capital Turin. A maid raised the alarm.
Police said the woman's daughter, 44-year-old Giovanna Anna Maria Boglione, had been taken in a state of shock to hospital where she was under guard.
"We can confirm that Mrs Boglione is suspected of the crime," a carabinieri paramilitary police spokesman said. He declined further comment.
Italian news agencies said Eleonara had been stabbed several times following an argument.

They said police had sealed off the villa, where reporters outside the gates had seen a cook and two servants leave in tears. The dead woman's daughter had separated from her husband and recently moved in with her mother, the agencies said.
Eleonara Maria Lancia was one of three children of Vincenzo Lancia, who died in 1937 when control of the car company he founded passed to his wife Adele, his former secretary.
Lancia, a former test driver for Fiat, founded the company in 1906, aged 25, with a friend and 50,000 lire in savings.

The name became a byword for luxury and racing cars and produced the sleek black Astura Lungo limousine which Fascist dictator Benito Mussolini had built especially for a visit to Italy in 1938 by Nazi Fuehrer Adolf Hitler.
The company sold a majority stake to the Pesenti financial group during hard times in 1955 and was on the verge of bankruptcy in 1969 when it was taken over by Fiat.
